passage:
Supervisor's note, cabin crew base. Written by Sachin.
Arohi joined our long-haul roster in January. I have watched how she handles the time changes and want to record it for new crew. She keeps the same sleep window at every hotel, whatever the local time, with blackout curtains and an eye mask, and she steps outside into morning light when she needs to wake up. She carries fruit and eats proper meals instead of living on snacks from the trolley. Last month she asked me to hold her answer on a transfer until she had slept, and she was right to. When tiredness and low mood did not lift, she booked a visit to the company doctor. What I did next: I asked Arohi to speak to the new crew on Friday.

qa.q: What does Arohi use at the hotel to protect her sleep window?
qa.a: Blackout curtains and an eye mask.

qa.q: Why did Arohi ask Sachin to hold her answer on the transfer?
qa.a: She was wary of trusting her own judgment while short of sleep and wanted to decide with a rested mind.

qa.q: What could new crew learn from Arohi's approach?
qa.a: Guard a fixed sleep window, use light and darkness on purpose, eat proper meals, delay big decisions until rested, and see a doctor when low mood does not lift.

qa.q: How does Sachin see Arohi's habits?
qa.a: Sachin respects them enough to record them as an example and asks Arohi to speak to the new crew.

grounding: Shows a person on a disrupted clock guarding a fixed sleep window, using light and darkness, eating sensibly, delaying a decision while tired and seeing a doctor when low mood persists.

Tuesday, 11:40 p.m.
Third week on the overseas support shift. Old Samir would have powered through on chai and fried snacks and then wondered why everything felt grey. New rules, and I kept every one today:
Slept nine to four with foil on the window and my phone in the other room. Ujjwal knows not to knock.
Went for a walk in the evening light before logging in, to tell my brain it's 'morning'.
Ate proper dal-rice at seven instead of chips.
My manager wanted an answer on the team-lead offer tonight. I said I'll reply on Friday, after my off days. Tired Samir says yes to everything.
If this heaviness doesn't lift, I'm booking the doctor. Promised Amma on the phone.

qa.q: What did Samir eat at seven?
What is Samir worried about when it comes to the team-lead offer?
qa.a: Samir is worried that a tired mind says yes to everything, so wants to decide after rest.

qa.q: Which of Samir's new rules seems most important, and why?
qa.a: Guarding the sleep window in a dark, quiet room, because steady sleep supports mood and judgment; the walk in the light also helps the body clock.

qa.q: What is it like for Ujjwal to share a home with Samir on these hours?
qa.a: Ujjwal has to stay quiet in the day and not knock, which takes patience but lets Samir sleep.

grounding: Shows a person on a night-time schedule guarding a fixed sleep window, using light and darkness on purpose, eating sensibly, delaying a big decision and planning to see a doctor if low mood persists.
